exposure: habits and frequency of drinking milk at night
outcome: dmft index (number of decayed, missing, filled primary teeth)
dmfs index (number of decayed, missing, filled primary tooth surfaces)
cohort: The study included 234 obese children and 234 normal children, aged 36 to 71 months, along with their mothers, from kindergartens in Hanoi, Vietnam.
finding: Obese children exhibited higher rates of early childhood caries, and specific eating habits and hobbies were identified as associated factors.
cross-section timing: When children were aged 36 to 71 months.
